title: Scope reduction for Structured Output v2 — alignment lanes & acceptance criteria
creator: Asha Patel
description: Reduce initial scope of Structured Output v2 to meet Q1 launch constraints while preserving core compatibility and measurable quality. Align engineering, design, and legal on what is deferred vs. gated-for-signoff; finalize acceptance lanes for a staged rollout (canary -> regional -> global).
acceptance_criteria: Design: final interaction mockups accepted by Design and PM (no visual regressions) and uploaded to Figma (link in artifacts)
Engineering: runtime behaviour conforms to trimmed schema subset (fields A, B, C) and passes performance SLOs: p95 latency <= 180ms on 8k token cache, throughput baseline met on dedicated pool
Engineering: end-to-end integration tests covering schema evolution paths and fallback behavior included in CI and green on main
Legal: export-control / data residency signoff for the trimmed feature set and any new telemetry collection documented
Console / Observability: per-route cost/latency breakdown and new eval dashboard populated with baseline prompts
Rollout: canary plan defined with metrics and automatic rollback thresholds (error rate > 3% OR latency regression > 20% sustained for 5m)
Docs & SDKs: prompt examples, structured-output schema docs and SDK validators published in docs.redwood.ai
Post-launch runbook: incident owner, triage steps, and customer communication templates prepared
comments: 2026-02-21: Kickoff sync — PM/Eng/Design/Legal present. Agreed to shrink initial schema to fields A/B/C and defer nested metadata until v2.1.
2026-02-25: Design review — DES feedback: clarify focus state for structured tokens; added two interaction variants. Action: DES to ship final mocks by 2026-03-05.
2026-03-01: Eng spike completed — prototype shows 12% CPU reduction with trimmed schema; noted edgecase with KV cache warming on model switch. ENG to add cache-warm metric and a mitigation flag.
2026-03-05: Legal review meeting — export-control questions around embedding exports. Legal requested example telemetry payload and retention policy; PM to provide by 2026-03-09.
2026-03-09: Provided telemetry payload sample and retention table. Legal: initial thumbs-up pending a short privacy review. Action: schedule privacy review in Cycle 11.
2026-03-12: Engineering submitted perf benchmark PR; current p95 = 172ms in dedicated staging which meets target. Next: wire observability and finalize canary thresholds.
decisions: Trimmed schema: fields A (primary text), B (structured tags), C (confidence) included. All other fields deferred to v2.1.
No new user-facing SDK changes in v2 GA; SDK validators to be introduced as opt-in in the first release
Canary rollout will be region-limited (US-west) for 48 hours before expanding to EU-east based on telemetry
next_steps: DES: finalize mocks and copy; deliver Figma link and accessibility checklist by 2026-03-14
ENG: complete integration tests and CI gating for schema evolution by 2026-03-18 (ENG ticket ENG-91234)
PM: coordinate privacy/legal signoff slot in Cycle 11 and prepare customer communication templates
Ops: create canary config in runtime and set alerting thresholds in Grafana/PagerDuty
blockers: Outstanding privacy review for telemetry payload (blocks Legal final signoff)
One flaky integration test related to KV cache warming (ENG-91234)
Need access to staging observability cluster for cost breakdown dashboards (infra ticket INF-4421)
notes: Aim: ship a conservative, compatible surface that reduces regression risk for existing customers who rely on structured output today.
Trade-off: deferring nested metadata reduces short-term developer frustration but requires clearer migration docs for v2.1.
If legal/privacy clearance slips beyond 2026-03-18 we will convert GA to a private-beta for affected regions.
